provenance: [REVIEWED] research/v3/ORACLE_QUESTION_SET.md v2 §A.6, schema group group-a.probes.v1. Probe wordings and the derivation are committed there before any inference exists.
design_notes: Group-a.probes.v1 is the DECOMPOSED-PROBE ARM: six independently meaningful yes/no/unsure probes whose aggregate derives the tag, instead of one six-way question. Reviewer-initiated, 2026-08-03: "might increase reliability, and make the questions easier to answer." Full design: ORACLE_QUESTION_SET.md §A.6.
Every probe passes the five-second rule standing alone, and every probe is meaningful on its own terms — none of them is the six-way question in disguise.

`enclosure` is NOT decomposed. It is group A's most reliable field already (raw 0.87, kappa 0.60 inter-variant [MEASURED premise-run-1]); decomposing a reliable question spends decode for nothing. It is also held first in both bundled variants, both because that is the position the measured A->B ordering gain came from and because holding one field constant across arms makes it a control: if enclosure moves in this arm, something about the arm changed the model, not the question.
Derivation is a priori and committed: `derivation.group-a.probes.v1.json` enumerates all 3^6 = 729 answer vectors. An implementation that disagrees with any entry is wrong, not the table.

Separate mode: one inference per probe, so no probe can see another probe's answer. This is the test of whether bundling contaminates — whether answering `one_colour: no` pushes the next answer. Its cost is the reason it is gated: see PREMISE_NEXT.md.

The stem, the option glosses and the framing paragraph are byte-identical to the bundled variants' rendering of this same probe. Only the surrounding questions are gone. If they were not identical the comparison would measure wording, not bundling.
deviations: No `confidence` field and no `note` field, in either mode. Under group-a.v1 both were degenerate: 298 of 299 parsed rows said `high` and the same 298 left the note empty [MEASURED premise-run-1]. In this arm the per-probe `unsure` value IS the confidence, asked at the granularity where it can act, and the aggregate uncertainty instruments are the inconsistency and tension rates from the derivation table. Re-adding `note` to the bundled variants is a one-line change if the reviewer wants the audit trail back.

`shading_direction` is asked unconditionally, with `not_applicable` available, rather than conditionally on a prior `shaded_field` answer. The derivation forces `not_applicable` when the derived ground_type is not shaded_field. In group-a.v1 the radial_or_vignette<->not_applicable pair was 21 of 26 inter-variant disagreements on this field [MEASURED premise-run-1]; the arm removes that class by construction.

This arm asks no question whose answer is `ground_type`. `ground_type` and `field_texture` are DERIVED, by the committed table in `derivation.group-a.probes.v1.json`. Nothing downstream may re-derive them a second way.

No probe quotes the corrected criterion or the canonical examples from ORACLE_QUESTION_SET.md §A.2. That is the point of the arm: importing the hard construct into an "easy question" would make it the same question in more words. Where a canonical case bears on one probe it appears as a local clarification of that probe alone (`separate_areas`: "A blurry or soft join still counts as two areas").
Separate mode carries no enclosure and no shading_direction: they are not probes, and the bundling question is about the probes. Those two fields come from the bundled arm.
system: You label album cover artwork for a research dataset. You answer only with the exact words offered. You never explain, never add fields, never use words that were not offered.
prompt:
Look at this album cover.

The BACKGROUND is the large area behind and around any subject, lettering or figures. Small details do not count. What the cover is about does not count. Whether it is attractive does not count.

One question only.

separate_areas - Can you point to two or more separate areas of the background, each with its own colour? A blurry or soft join still counts as two areas.
   yes - two or more separate areas, each its own colour
   no - you cannot pick out separate areas
   unsure - you cannot tell

Reply with JSON only.
